claim: BioID2 proximity labeling employs the promiscuous BirA2, which attaches biotin molecules to the lysines of proteins within an approximate distance of 10 nm.
source: BioID2 employs the promiscuous BirA2, which attaches biotin molecules to the lysines of proteins within an approximate distance of 10 nm (Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2016, which is the source describing the BioID2 technology.

claim: Transgenic zebrafish expressing BirA2-GFP under the cmlc2 promoter show BirA2-GFP distributed throughout the cytoplasm and nuclei of adult cardiomyocytes.
source: BirA2-GFP was readily detected in adult zebrafish cardiac chambers, where it was distributed throughout the cytoplasm and nuclei of adult cardiomyocytes (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by direct observation described in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Effective protein biotinylation in zebrafish cardiomyocytes occurred only when biotin was delivered by intraperitoneal injection, not by aquarium water.
source: We found that effective protein biotinylation occurred only when biotin was delivered by injection (Figure 1D, E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D, E and supplementary figures.

claim: BirA2-GFP-CAAX localizes to the membranes of cardiomyocytes in transgenic zebrafish.
source: We found that the majority of BirA2-GFP-CAAX signal associated with the cardiomyocyte plasma membrane in cmlc2:birA2-GFP-CAAX hearts (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 1C and supplementary figures.

claim: Quantitative BioID2 analysis captured 1113 distinct proteins in adult zebrafish cardiomyocytes.
source: Quantitative BioID2 analysis captured 1113 distinct proteins, of which 343 proteins showed a 2.5-fold enrichment in BirA2-CAAX samples when compared to BirA2-GFP samples (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative mass spectrometry data reported in the manuscript.

claim: 343 proteins showed a 2.5-fold enrichment in BirA2-CAAX samples compared to BirA2-GFP samples.
source: Quantitative BioID2 analysis captured 1113 distinct proteins, of which 343 proteins showed a 2.5-fold enrichment in BirA2-CAAX samples when compared to BirA2-GFP samples (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: Gene ontology analysis of the 343 proteins enriched in BirA2-CAAX samples revealed enrichment for proteins associated with cellular junctions, plasma membrane, and membrane-bound organelles.
source: Gene ontology analysis for cellular components of the 343 proteins revealed enrichment for proteins associated with cellular junctions, plasma membrane, and membrane-bound organelles (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis results shown in Figure 1H.

claim: In vivo proximity labeling using BioID2 is functional in zebrafish and can profile proteomes of highly specialized cells like cardiomyocytes.
source: Our results indicate that in vivo proximity labeling using BioID2 is functional in zebrafish and can profile proteomes of highly specialized cells like cardiomyocytes.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Proliferation of cardiomyocytes in the tamoxifen-inducible diphtheria toxin A ablation model is most prominent around 7 days post incubation.
source: Proliferation of cardiomyocytes in this injury model is most prominent around 7 dpi, with regeneration of the myocardium essentially complete by 28 dpi (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Regeneration of the myocardium is essentially complete by 28 days post incubation in the cardiomyocyte ablation model.
source: Proliferation of cardiomyocytes in this injury model is most prominent around 7 dpi, with regeneration of the myocardium essentially complete by 28 dpi (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations shown in supplementary figures.

claim: 208 proteins showed a 1.5-fold or greater change during regeneration when compared to uninjured hearts in cmlc2:bira2-GFP hearts.
source: Quantitative mass spectrometry analysis of pooled samples revealed that 208 proteins showed a 1.5-fold or greater change during regeneration when compared to uninjured hearts (Figure 2D, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative mass spectrometry data.

claim: Most proteins with changed levels during regeneration in the whole-cell BioID2 assay increased rather than decreased.
source: Of these, most protein levels increase during heart regeneration.
evidence: The claim is supported by the heat map analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Proteins with increased levels during regeneration in the whole-cell BioID2 set are involved in wound healing, cardiac development, muscle cell differentiation, and response to wounding.
source: Gene ontology analysis (over-representation test) for biological processes characterized the proteins with increased levels during regeneration in the whole-cell BioID2 set as involved in wound healing, cardiac development, muscle cell differentiation, and response to wounding, whereas decreased proteins were enriched for metabolites and energy precursors (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis results shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Proteins with decreased levels during regeneration in the whole-cell BioID2 set were enriched for metabolites and energy precursors.
source: Gene ontology analysis (over-representation test) for biological processes characterized the proteins with increased levels during regeneration in the whole-cell BioID2 set as involved in wound healing, cardiac development, muscle cell differentiation, and response to wounding, whereas decreased proteins were enriched for metabolites and energy precursors (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis results shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The top 10% of increased proteins in the whole-cell BioID2 assay included ErbB2 and the mTOR signaling protein Rictora.
source: The top 10% of increased proteins included ErbB2 and the mTOR signaling protein Rictora (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), each previously implicated in heart regeneration (Gemberling et al., 2015; Sciarretta et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and citations to previous studies.

claim: ErbB2 and Rictora have been previously implicated in heart regeneration.
source: The top 10% of increased proteins included ErbB2 and the mTOR signaling protein Rictora (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), each previously implicated in heart regeneration (Gemberling et al., 2015; Sciarretta et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gemberling et al., 2015 and Sciarretta et al., 2015.

claim: 173 proteins showed a 1.5-fold or greater change in membrane-associated proteins during regeneration in cmlc2:bira2-GFP-CAAX samples.
source: We identified 173 proteins with a 1.5-fold or greater change in membrane-associated proteins during regeneration when normalized to uninjured hearts (Figure 2C, E, Supplementary file 3), with the majority of these proteins reducing presence during regeneration.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative mass spectrometry data.

claim: The majority of proteins with changed levels in the membrane BioID2 assay reduced presence during regeneration.
source: We identified 173 proteins with a 1.5-fold or greater change in membrane-associated proteins during regeneration when normalized to uninjured hearts (Figure 2C, E, Supplementary file 3), with the majority of these proteins reducing presence during regeneration.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Proteins with reduced membrane levels during regeneration showed over-representation of involvement in transmembrane transport, muscle development, and energy production.
source: Proteins with reduced membrane levels during regeneration showed over-representation of involvement in transmembrane transport, muscle development, and energy production (electron transport and glycolysis), while proteins increased at the membrane during regeneration were involved in protein complex assembly and organelle organization (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis results shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Proteins increased at the membrane during regeneration were involved in protein complex assembly and organelle organization.
source: Proteins with reduced membrane levels during regeneration showed over-representation of involvement in transmembrane transport, muscle development, and energy production (electron transport and glycolysis), while proteins increased at the membrane during regeneration were involved in protein complex assembly and organelle organization (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis results shown in Figure 2E.

claim: 44 proteins were shared between BirA2-GFP and BirA2-GFP-CAAX data sets.
source: Comparison of proteins found in BirA2-GFP and BirA2-GFP-CAAX data sets identified 44 shared proteins (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of the two data sets shown in Figure 2C.

claim: 16 proteins showed opposing changes in levels at the membrane or in the whole cell among the 44 shared proteins.
source: Of these, 16 proteins showed opposing changes in levels at the membrane or in the whole cell (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Epb41l5 was predominantly localized at the plasma membrane in uninjured hearts and increased presence throughout cardiomyocytes during regeneration.
source: Epb41l5 was predominantly localized at the plasma membrane (Figure 2G, arrows) and increased presence throughout cardiomyocytes during regeneration, consistent with the BioID2 data.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Epb41l5 is involved in animal organ development and has been implicated as a positive regulator of Notch signaling.
source: Erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 like 5 (Epb41l5) is involved in animal organ development and has been implicated as a positive regulator of Notch signaling, a pathway involved in heart regeneration (Matsuda et al., 2016; Zhao et al., 2014, Figure 2F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Matsuda et al., 2016 and Zhao et al., 2014.

claim: Notch signaling is a pathway involved in heart regeneration.
source: Erythrocyte membrane protein band 4.1 like 5 (Epb41l5) is involved in animal organ development and has been implicated as a positive regulator of Notch signaling, a pathway involved in heart regeneration (Matsuda et al., 2016; Zhao et al., 2014, Figure 2F, G).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Matsuda et al., 2016 and Zhao et al., 2014.

claim: Talin 2 is an adapter protein that couples integrin focal adhesions to the actin cytoskeleton.
source: Talin 2, an adapter protein that couples integrin focal adhesions to the actin cytoskeleton (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, B), displayed low levels in uninjured hearts (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Talin 2 function.

claim: Talin 2 displayed low levels in uninjured hearts and increased levels near the wound site and in ventricular muscle away from the injury upon injury.
source: Talin 2, an adapter protein that couples integrin focal adhesions to the actin cytoskeleton (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, B), displayed low levels in uninjured hearts (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B). Upon injury, Talin 2 levels increased near the wound site as well as in ventricular muscle away from the injury, with a punctate pattern appearing that resembled focal adhesions (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Seta levels were undetectable in uninjured hearts and became prominent in compact muscle and epicardial tissue in injured ventricles.
source: Seta levels were undetectable in uninjured hearts, yet became prominent in compact muscle and epicardial tissue in injured ventricles (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2H and supplementary figures.

claim: Seta signal was perinuclear and colocalized with wheat germ agglutinin, indicating that Seta associates in part with the nuclear membrane and endomembranes after heart injury.
source: The Seta signal was perinuclear and colocalized with wheat germ agglutinin (WGA), which indicates that Seta associates in part with the nuclear membrane and endomembranes after heart injury (Figure 2H, arrows, Figure 2—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing colocalization with WGA.

claim: Seta has been proposed to silence histone acetyltransferase-dependent transcription.
source: As Seta has been proposed to silence histone acetyltransferase-dependent transcription, its recruitment to nuclear and endomembranes could impact this function (Seo et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Seo et al., 2001.

claim: BioID2 can capture changes in the proteomes of cardiomyocytes during heart regeneration.
source: Taken together, our data indicate that BioID2 can capture changes in the proteomes of cardiomyocytes during heart regeneration, providing a resource for candidate effectors.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nrg1 ligand binds its receptor ErbB4 on cardiomyocytes, causing heterodimerization of Erbb4 and its co-receptor ErbB2.
source: Nrg1 ligand has been reported to bind its receptor ErbB4 on cardiomyocytes, causing heterodimerization of Erbb4 and its co-receptor ErbB2 (Bersell et al., 2009; Harskamp et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bersell et al., 2009 and Harskamp et al., 2016.

claim: Quantitative mass spectrometry analysis of ErbB2-BirA2-HA hearts identified 667 proteins.
source: Quantitative mass spectrometry analysis identified 667 proteins, of which 108 showed a >1.5-fold change during regeneration when normalized to uninjured control hearts (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative mass spectrometry data.

claim: 108 proteins showed a >1.5-fold change during regeneration in the ErbB2-BirA2-HA data set when normalized to uninjured control hearts.
source: Quantitative mass spectrometry analysis identified 667 proteins, of which 108 showed a >1.5-fold change during regeneration when normalized to uninjured control hearts (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative mass spectrometry data.

claim: Nine known ErbB2 interactors were identified in the ErbB2-BirA2-HA BioID2 data set.
source: Using STRING and BioGRID databases, we identified nine known ErbB2 interactors in our data set.
evidence: The claim is supported by database searches of the BioID2 data.

claim: Three known ErbB2 interactors showed increased association with ErbB2 during regeneration.
source: Three of these proteins showed increased association with ErbB2 during regeneration, whereas two had decreased association (Figure 3C, yellow and blue circles, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Two known ErbB2 interactors had decreased association with ErbB2 during regeneration.
source: Three of these proteins showed increased association with ErbB2 during regeneration, whereas two had decreased association (Figure 3C, yellow and blue circles, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Overall expression levels of ErbB2 interactors were not predictive of ErbB2 association.
source: Next, we examined the levels of these candidates as reported in published transcriptome and proteome data sets (Goldman et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2018; Kang et al., 2016; Ben-Yair et al., 2019), and found that overall expression levels were not predictive of ErbB2 association (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison with published transcriptome and proteome data sets.

claim: The strongest detected increase in ErbB2 association was with the Rho GTPase Rho A-b.
source: The strongest detected increase was an association with the Rho GTPase Rho A-b, and pathway analyses indicated enrichment for proteins involved in cytoskeletal regulation by Rho GTPases (Figure 3C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by BioID2 data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Pathway analyses of the ErbB2-BirA2-HA data set indicated enrichment for proteins involved in cytoskeletal regulation by Rho GTPases.
source: The strongest detected increase was an association with the Rho GTPase Rho A-b, and pathway analyses indicated enrichment for proteins involved in cytoskeletal regulation by Rho GTPases (Figure 3C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by pathway analysis results shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Rho A activation by ErbB2 has been previously reported to promote pro-metastatic and invasive behavior of human breast cancer cells.
source: Rho A activation by ErbB2 has been previously reported to promote pro-metastatic and invasive behavior of human breast cancer cells and contribute to mammary adenocarcinoma tumorigenesis (Brantley-Sieders et al., 2008; Worzfeld et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Brantley-Sieders et al., 2008 and Worzfeld et al., 2012.

claim: Rho A activation by ErbB2 has been previously reported to contribute to mammary adenocarcinoma tumorigenesis.
source: Rho A activation by ErbB2 has been previously reported to promote pro-metastatic and invasive behavior of human breast cancer cells and contribute to mammary adenocarcinoma tumorigenesis (Brantley-Sieders et al., 2008; Worzfeld et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Brantley-Sieders et al., 2008 and Worzfeld et al., 2012.

claim: A recent study implicated Rho A mislocalization with aberrant spindle orientation leading to binucleation, a common feature of mammalian cardiomyocytes that is thought to inhibit cardiomyocyte proliferation.
source: Moreover, a recent study implicated Rho A mislocalization with aberrant spindle orientation leading to binucleation, a common feature of mammalian CMs that is thought to inhibit cardiomyocytes (CM) proliferation (Leone et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Leone et al., 2018.

claim: Rho A was pulled down with ErbB2-BirA2-HA in regenerating heart samples, but not from uninjured myocardium.
source: Interestingly, Rho A was pulled down with ErbB2-BirA2-HA in regenerating heart samples, but not from uninjured myocardium, suggesting a context-dependent association (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: ErbB2-Rho A association is context-dependent, increasing during regeneration.
source: Interestingly, Rho A was pulled down with ErbB2-BirA2-HA in regenerating heart samples, but not from uninjured myocardium, suggesting a context-dependent association (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation results showing differential association in regenerating vs. uninjured hearts.

claim: All known Rho A interactors detected in the cmlc2:birA2-GFP data set showed elevated levels after injury.
source: Yet, all known Rho A interactors detected in our cmlc2:birA2-GFP data set showed elevated levels after injury, including ErbB2 (59.2-fold; Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: ErbB2 levels increased 59.2-fold after injury in the cmlc2:birA2-GFP data set.
source: Yet, all known Rho A interactors detected in our cmlc2:birA2-GFP data set showed elevated levels after injury, including ErbB2 (59.2-fold; Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: ROCK2a levels were elevated in the whole-cell BioID2 data set during regeneration.
source: ROCK2a levels were elevated in our whole-cell BioID2 data set, further confirmed by western blotting (Figure 3G), consistent with the idea that ErbB2–Rho A association could impact ROCK2 levels in cardiomyocytes after injury.
evidence: The claim is supported by BioID2 data and western blot analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Rho A signaling is known to facilitate cytoskeletal changes via Rho-associated protein kinases (ROCK).
source: Rho A signaling is known to facilitate cytoskeletal changes via Rho-associated protein kinases (ROCK), which have been reported to regulate the DNA binding activity of the cardiogenic transcription factor Gata4 and nuclear localization of SRF in cell culture (Kaarbo et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2003; Yanazume et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kaarbo et al., 2013, Liu et al., 2003, and Yanazume et al., 2002.

claim: ROCK has been reported to regulate the DNA binding activity of the cardiogenic transcription factor Gata4 in cell culture.
source: Rho A signaling is known to facilitate cytoskeletal changes via Rho-associated protein kinases (ROCK), which have been reported to regulate the DNA binding activity of the cardiogenic transcription factor Gata4 and nuclear localization of SRF in cell culture (Kaarbo et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2003; Yanazume et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kaarbo et al., 2013, Liu et al., 2003, and Yanazume et al., 2002.

claim: ROCK has been reported to regulate nuclear localization of SRF in cell culture.
source: Rho A signaling is known to facilitate cytoskeletal changes via Rho-associated protein kinases (ROCK), which have been reported to regulate the DNA binding activity of the cardiogenic transcription factor Gata4 and nuclear localization of SRF in cell culture (Kaarbo et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2003; Yanazume et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kaarbo et al., 2013, Liu et al., 2003, and Yanazume et al., 2002.

claim: Treatment with the Rho A inhibitor Rhosin reduced the cardiomyocyte proliferation index by approximately 68% after partial ventricular resection.
source: In these experiments, Rhosin reduced the proliferation index by ~68% (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Animals expressing a dominant-negative Rho A for 30 days after resection had injury sites that remained deficient in cardiac myofibers, whereas control hearts had re-established a contiguous wall of muscle.
source: In animals expressing a dominant-negative Rho A for 30 days after resection (Figure 4F), injury sites remained deficient in cardiac myofibers, whereas in control hearts had re-established a contiguous wall of muscle (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Rac1 and Cdc42 are similarly required for normal heart regeneration.
source: Using inducible dominant-negative gene cassettes in transgenic animals, we found that Rac1 and Cdc42 are similarly required for normal heart regeneration (Figure 4F, middle and bottom panels).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Rho A, Rac1, and Cdc42 are each implicated in zebrafish heart regeneration.
source: Thus, our data implicate each member of the small GTPase trio – Rho A, Rac1, and Cdc42 – in zebrafish heart regeneration.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Hearts that ectopically expressed Nrg1 for 14 days showed an approximately 85% increase in total Rho A protein.
source: We examined Rho A levels from hearts that ectopically expressed Nrg1 for 14 days, and unlike during ablation-induced heart regeneration where Rho A levels are unchanged, we found an ~85% increase in total Rho A protein (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,mB).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: During ablation-induced heart regeneration, Rho A levels are unchanged.
source: We examined Rho A levels from hearts that ectopically expressed Nrg1 for 14 days, and unlike during ablation-induced heart regeneration where Rho A levels are unchanged, we found an ~85% increase in total Rho A protein (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,mB).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of western blot data.

claim: Three daily injections of zebrafish with Rhosin reduced the cardiomyocyte proliferation index by approximately 71% in the presence of ectopic Nrg1 expression.
source: Consistent with a mitogenic role, three daily injections of zebrafish with Rhosin reduced the cardiomyocyte proliferation index by ~71% in the presence of ectopic Nrg1 expression (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B–D.

claim: Vegfaa-expressing hearts had elevated cardiac Rho A levels.
source: Western blot analysis revealed that vegfaa-expressing hearts had elevated cardiac Rho A levels, whereas alfacalcidol-treated hearts displayed no significant change (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Alfacalcidol-treated hearts displayed no significant change in Rho A levels.
source: Western blot analysis revealed that vegfaa-expressing hearts had elevated cardiac Rho A levels, whereas alfacalcidol-treated hearts displayed no significant change (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Inhibition of Rho A by Rhosin reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation by approximately 68% during vegfaa overexpression.
source: Inhibition of Rho A by Rhosin reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation by ~68% and ~65% during vegfaa overexpression and alfacalcidol treatment, respectively (Figure 5E–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E–H.

claim: Inhibition of Rho A by Rhosin reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation by approximately 65% during alfacalcidol treatment.
source: Inhibition of Rho A by Rhosin reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation by ~68% and ~65% during vegfaa overexpression and alfacalcidol treatment, respectively (Figure 5E–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E–H.

claim: Rho A signaling is a major target during heart regeneration, required for normal cardiomyocyte proliferation in response to injury or presence of Nrg1, Vegfaa, or vitamin D.
source: Thus, our data indicate that Rho A signaling is a major target during heart regeneration, required for normal cardiomyocyte proliferation in response to injury or presence of Nrg1, Vegfaa, or vitamin D.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Published single-cell RNA-seq data revealed detectable rhoaa expression in cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and immune cells during zebrafish heart regeneration.
source: Assessment of published single-cell RNA-seq data revealed detectable rhoaa expression in cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and immune cells, and rhoab expression in cardiomyocytes and endothelial cells during zebrafish heart regeneration (Supplementary file 6; Honkoop et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data from Honkoop et al., 2019.

claim: Published single-cell RNA-seq data revealed detectable rhoab expression in cardiomyocytes and endothelial cells during zebrafish heart regeneration.
source: Assessment of published single-cell RNA-seq data revealed detectable rhoaa expression in cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and immune cells, and rhoab expression in cardiomyocytes and endothelial cells during zebrafish heart regeneration (Supplementary file 6; Honkoop et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data from Honkoop et al., 2019.

claim: Published profiles of cardiomyocyte H3.3 occupancy indicate an approximately twofold increase in H3.3 enrichment in rhoaa and rhoab gene bodies during heart regeneration.
source: Additionally, published profiles of cardiomyocyte H3.3 occupancy (Goldman et al., 2017), an indicator of active gene expression, indicate an approximately twofold increase in H3.3 enrichment in rhoaa and rhoab gene bodies during heart regeneration (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of published H3.3 occupancy data from Goldman et al., 2017.

claim: RNA-seq data from ventricles after 7 days of induced myocardial Nrg1 overexpression revealed that rhoaa levels were weakly elevated (1.6-fold).
source: Generation of RNA-seq data from ventricles of transgenic animals after 7 days of induced myocardial Nrg1 overexpression (see Materials and methods) revealed that rhoaa levels were weakly elevated (1.6-fold), whereas no changes in rhoab or rhoac were detectable (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data generated in this study.

claim: RNA-seq data from ventricles after 7 days of induced myocardial Nrg1 overexpression revealed no changes in rhoab or rhoac levels.
source: Generation of RNA-seq data from ventricles of transgenic animals after 7 days of induced myocardial Nrg1 overexpression (see Materials and methods) revealed that rhoaa levels were weakly elevated (1.6-fold), whereas no changes in rhoab or rhoac were detectable (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data generated in this study.

claim: rhoaa and rhoab are top candidates for Rho A function in cardiomyocytes.
source: Thus, rhoaa and rhoab are top candidates for Rho A function in cardiomyocytes, although conditional disruption of the rhoa genes in zebrafish is needed to distinguish which member(s) is key.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the expression data and functional studies presented.

claim: BioID2 profiling for interactors with ErbB2 implicated Rho A as a target of ErbB2 signaling in cardiomyocytes.
source: BioID2 profiling for interactors with ErbB2, a co-receptor for the cardiomyocyte mitogen Nrg1, implicated Rho A as a target of ErbB2 signaling in cardiomyocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by the BioID2 data showing increased association between ErbB2 and Rho A during regeneration.

claim: Blockade of Rho A during heart regeneration disrupted muscle creation.
source: Blockade of Rho A during heart regeneration, or during cardiogenic stimulation by the mitogenic influences Nrg1, Vegfaa, or vitamin D, disrupted muscle creation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing impaired regeneration with Rho A inhibition.

claim: Blockade of Rho A during cardiogenic stimulation by Nrg1, Vegfaa, or vitamin D disrupted muscle creation.
source: Blockade of Rho A during heart regeneration, or during cardiogenic stimulation by the mitogenic influences Nrg1, Vegfaa, or vitamin D, disrupted muscle creation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing reduced cardiomyocyte proliferation with Rho A inhibition during mitogen treatment.

claim: Proximity labeling is a useful resource to interrogate cell proteomes and signaling networks during tissue regeneration in zebrafish.
source: Our findings reveal proximity labeling as a useful resource to interrogate cell proteomes and signaling networks during tissue regeneration in zebrafish.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the successful application of BioID2 in this study.

claim: Zebrafish regenerate cardiac muscle after injury with minimal scar formation, based on division of pre-existing cardiomyocytes.
source: Unlike mammals, teleost zebrafish regenerate cardiac muscle after injury with minimal scar formation, based on division of pre-existing cardiomyocytes (Poss et al., 2002; Kikuchi et al., 2010; Jopling et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Poss et al., 2002, Kikuchi et al., 2010, and Jopling et al., 2010.

claim: Heart regeneration in zebrafish is a relentless process that outcompetes scarring to recover heart function.
source: Evidence to date indicates that heart regeneration in zebrafish is a relentless process that outcompetes scarring to recover the heart function, rather than a linear series of molecular steps and synchronized cellular progressions.
evidence: The claim is based on accumulated evidence about zebrafish heart regeneration.

claim: Three secreted factors, Nrg1, Vegfaa, and vitamin D, have been demonstrated to have instructive mitogenic effects on cardiomyocytes in zebrafish.
source: Three secreted factors, Nrg1, Vegfaa, and vitamin D, have been demonstrated to have instructive mitogenic effects, characterized by the ability to induce cardiomyocyte proliferation in zebrafish in the absence of injury (Gemberling et al., 2015; Karra et al., 2018; Han et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gemberling et al., 2015, Karra et al., 2018, and Han et al., 2019.

claim: Nrg1, Vegfaa, and vitamin D can induce cardiomyocyte proliferation in zebrafish in the absence of injury.
source: Three secreted factors, Nrg1, Vegfaa, and vitamin D, have been demonstrated to have instructive mitogenic effects, characterized by the ability to induce cardiomyocyte proliferation in zebrafish in the absence of injury (Gemberling et al., 2015; Karra et al., 2018; Han et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gemberling et al., 2015, Karra et al., 2018, and Han et al., 2019.

claim: Nrg1/ErbB2 signaling can stimulate cardiomyocyte division in adult mice, most notably when ErbB2 is experimentally expressed in the form of a ligand-independent activator.
source: Nrg1/ErbB2 signaling can stimulate cardiomyocyte division in adult mice, most notably when ErbB2 is experimentally expressed in the form of a ligand-independent activator (Bersell et al., 2009; D'Uva et al., 2015; Gordon et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bersell et al., 2009, D'Uva et al., 2015, and Gordon et al., 2009.

claim: ErbB2 signaling was recently reported to work in part through regulation of YAP in cardiomyocytes.
source: ErbB2 signaling was recently reported to work in part through regulation of YAP, a transcriptional activator that can impact cytoskeletal remodeling and cell division in cardiomyocytes during cardiac growth or repair in mice (Leach et al., 2017; Aharonov et al., 2020; Heallen et al., 2013; Heallen et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Leach et al., 2017, Aharonov et al., 2020, Heallen et al., 2013, and Heallen et al., 2011.

claim: In zebrafish, Nrg1/ErbB2 signals in part by promoting glycolysis versus mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation.
source: In zebrafish, Nrg1/ErbB2 signals in part by promoting glycolysis versus mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and reducing Tp53 levels through upregulation of its inhibitor Mdm2 (Shoffner et al., 2020; Honkoop et al., 2019; Fukuda et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Shoffner et al., 2020, Honkoop et al., 2019, and Fukuda et al., 2019.

claim: In zebrafish, Nrg1/ErbB2 signals in part by reducing Tp53 levels through upregulation of its inhibitor Mdm2.
